name: printenv
description: Prints environment variables — all of them, or specific ones.

flags.description: Print the value of NAME only (empty output and exit code 1 if unset).

examples.explanation: Prints just the value of HOME.
The script pattern for required variables — printenv exits nonzero for unset names, so it works in conditions too.

about: printenv prints only EXPORTED variables (the environment), unlike set which also shows shell-local variables and functions. It is part of coreutils, so it works identically in scripts and cron where shell builtins may not.
useCases: Verify what a cron job or service actually receives.
mistakes: Using printenv to find shell-local variables — use set or declare -p for those.
